trigger: 3-node mini cluster. The leader's processing of the ACKs for create H is delayed. Follower F restarts and gets TRUNC(H-1). The leader's startForwarding for F is delayed while H commits, so F's sync stream is TRUNC, PROPOSAL(H), COMMIT(H), NEWLEADER. F's connection to the leader is lost at the NEWLEADER read (injected SocketException at the Learner.readPacket I/O boundary). F rejoins in the same JVM, logs H+1 and H+2, and later restarts.
reason: In TRUNC/SNAP sync, snapshotNeeded = true, so writeToTxnLog is false. COMMITs that arrive before NEWLEADER are only applied in memory (zk.processTxn, Learner.java:683-692), and the NEWLEADER snapshot (Learner.java:759-760) is what persists them. When the sync aborts before NEWLEADER is processed, Learner.shutdown calls zk.shutdown(syncMode == SNAP) (Learner.java:924). TRUNC is not SNAP, so the in-memory DB is kept (ZooKeeperServer.java:928-946; fastForwardDataBase cannot drop H). F then registers with lastZxid H taken from memory (QuorumPeer.getLastLoggedZxid, QuorumPeer.java:1390), gets an empty DIFF, and appends H+1 onward to a new log file. Its durable history now permanently lacks the committed txn H. On restart, replay goes from H-1 straight to H+1, and ZKDatabase.addCommittedProposal throws at ZKDatabase.java:341, so F cannot start. Every step is allowed: a restart, delays the real scheduler or network can produce (LearnerHandler startForwarding is called after the TRUNC is queued, LearnerHandler.java:864/925), and a lost connection during sync. The check is correctly catching corruption that the sync protocol produced.
summary: A TRUNC-mode sync interrupted before NEWLEADER leaves a committed txn applied only in memory. The follower rejoins with it, so its on-disk log has a permanent hole and the server fails to load its database on the next restart.
